title: Midday throughput dip investigation and autoscaler sanity notes
content:
Summary:

Observed a repeatable midday (~11:30-13:15 UTC) drop in throughput for Dedicated GPU pools serving customer workloads. Drop manifests as a ~30-40% reduction in requests/sec sustained for ~45–90 minutes, with p95 latency rising and request queuing on the API side. No single tenant accounted for the entire drop window.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture rapid-fire on-call notes, commands run, and temporary mitigations used to restore capacity.
- Record hypotheses that were surfaced and how we validated/refuted them.
- Draft a short, testable runbook for similar future incidents and list follow-up engineering tasks.

High-level timeline (local times UTC):
- 2025-02-12 11:28 — First automated alert: pool-throughput-deviation (p50 down 28%)
- 2025-02-12 11:32 — Oncall acknowledged; started signal correlation (metrics, logs, autoscaler events)
- 2025-02-12 11:36 — Noticed scale-controller leader flapping entries in controller logs (re-election every ~60s)
- 2025-02-12 11:42 — Manual scale up attempted (adjust desired to +20%) — transient improvement
- 2025-02-12 12:10 — Throughput dipped again; observed KV cache hit-rate drop on some model shards
- 2025-02-12 12:34 — Drained 2 candidate nodes suspected of having thermal throttling; throughput recovered slowly
- 2025-02-12 12:50 — Replaced scale-controller image with canary containing leader-election logging patch (hotfix), observed leader stability
- 2025-02-12 13:15 — System returned to normal baseline; alerts closed

Metrics + signals examined (queries used in investigation):
- PromQL: rate(inference_requests_total[5m]) by (pool) — showed ~35% drop for pool-gamma
- PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
- Node exporter: gpu_temperature_celsius gauge by instance — small transient spikes on 2 hosts
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[5m])) by (shard) — notable drop from 92% -> 61% for shards 7–9
- Controller logs: grep leader_election /var/log/scale-controller.log — showed repeated renew failures

Immediate hypotheses and how we checked them:
1) Autoscaler/scale-controller flapping -> delayed scale-up and insufficient capacity
   - Evidence: leader-election errors + scaledown/supression events around incident.
   - Action: patched controller to include extended logging, temporarily bumped controller replicas to 3 to reduce single-leader blast radius.
   - Result: leader stable, scaling decisions were applied faster on the next spike.

2) Under-reported resource requests for inference sidecars; scheduler oversubscription
   - Evidence: scheduler reported some pods with lower resource request than actual consumption (mis-specified requests in older rollout).
   - Action: inspected recent rollout PRs — found a default request tweak merged 2025-02-08. Started canary to rollback that change in one pool.
   - Result: rollback pool regained normal scheduling headroom; throughput improved for the canary subset.

3) KV cache invalidation/amplification after a model shard refresh created extra cold-start CPU/GPU work
   - Evidence: KV cache hit-rate dropped for shards 7–9 coincident with dip; logs show LRU evictions > 95th percentile.
   - Action: forced warmup for affected shards by replaying a small representative prompt set to repopulate KV caches.
   - Result: recovery observed within 12–18 minutes for warmed shards.

4) Hardware-level thermal or firmware-induced throttling on a small subset of GPUs
   - Evidence: two hosts showed transient GPU temp spikes and lowered clock rates in vendor telemetry.
   - Action: drained hosts, coordinated with infra to inspect firmware, collected dmesg and nvidia-smi logs.
   - Result: one host later required a firmware microcode bump and replacement under warranty; removal reduced risk.

Commands & quick checks used during triage (examples):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated -o wide --selector=pool=pool-gamma
- kubectl logs -n infra -lapp=scale-controller --tail=200 | grep leader_election
- prometheus query examples (via grafana/explore): rate(inference_requests_total[5m]) by (pool)
- ssh root@gpu-host-42 -- sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.current.graphics --format=csv
- redis-cli -h kvcache-shard-7 INFO keyspace | grep keys

Temporary mitigations executed (order matters):
1) Increased desired replicas for pool-gamma by +20% to absorb immediate backlog
2) Bumped scale-controller replica count from 1 -> 3 to reduce leader churn probability
3) Drained and cordoned two suspect hosts (gpu-host-42, gpu-host-47) during low-traffic window; rotated workloads off
4) Warmed KV caches for shards with low hit-rate using a replay harness (safe, read-only)
5) Rolled back the resource-request change as a canary in pool-delta

Effectiveness: the combination of scale-controller stabilization and cache warmup produced the most measurable improvement; hardware drains removed a recurring source of intermittent throttling.

Runbook sketch (for future incidents labeled: midday-throughput-dip):
1) Detection: alert when pool throughput is down >20% for 10m AND p95 latency increased by >30%
2) Initial triage (first 10m):
   - Check scale-controller health: kubectl get pods -n infra -lapp=scale-controller
   - Query Prometheus for per-pool throughput and per-shard cache hit-rate
   - Check node GPU temp/clock telemetry for any hot hosts
3) Quick mitigations (apply if confirmed):
   - Temporarily increase desired replicas for impacted pool by +20%
   - If leader election errors are observed, scale controller replicas to 3 and enable debug logging
   - If cache hit-rate < 75% for >15m, trigger safe cache-warm replay for affected shards
4) Escalation: page SRE oncall + infra oncall if hardware telemetry shows thermal/clock throttling or if leader election persists after increasing controller replicas
5) Post-incident: collect controller logs, node telemetry, and KV cache metrics; create postmortem ticket within 48 hours

Post-incident follow-ups / action items (owner -> brief plan):
- Asha M. -> Draft and land scale-controller liveness/leader-election metrics (SRE-5172)
- Miguel S. -> Add canary test for resource-request drift in CI (infra PR to add e2e scheduling checks)
- Priya K. -> Implement an automated cache warmup job that can be invoked by the runbook (design doc due 2025-03-01)
- Infra Team -> Replace/firmware patch host gpu-host-42 and add kernel-level counters to detect early throttling (ticket INFRA-289)

Open questions we couldn't fully answer in-shift:
- Why did KV cache hit-rate drop on shards 7–9 specifically? (query patterns, imbalance, or a reshuffle during a background rebalancer?)
- Was there any hidden interaction between controller leader flapping and the scheduler's perceived capacity (race that amplified scale controller decisions)?
- Could a user workload pattern (e.g., synthetic bursts from internal load tests) have coincided and made a minor problem surface as a larger incident? Check internal load test schedule.

Notes to follow-up investigators:
- Pull controller logs for the 24h window around 2025-02-12 from Loki: label app=scale-controller, include leader-election and reconcile loop durations.
- Export Prometheus timeseries for kv_cache_hits/requests by shard and correlate with model deployment events (Git tags/rollouts).
- Compare node-level GPU clocks and PCIe errors across the affected hosts. Look for shared infra events (power cycles, maintenance jobs) in cloud-provider audit logs.

Appendix: quick reference snippets for runbook insertion
- Detection query (PromQL):
  sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) by (pool) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[6h])) by (pool) < 0.75
- Cache warmup command (internal tool):
  /opt/tools/kvcache-warmup --shard=7 --profile=representative_prompts --dry-run=false
- Controller sanity check: kubectl exec -n infra deploy/scale-controller -- /bin/scalectl status | jq

Quick retrospective notes (what went well / what to improve):
- Good: rapid cross-team communication, effective temporary mitigations (cache warmup + controller stabilization), oncall used evidence-driven steps.
- Improve: need automated tests to catch resource-request drift before rollouts, better preflight for scale-controller leader-election under noisy environments, and an automated cache-warmup primitive.

Document history:
- 2025-02-12 initial incident notes (Asha M.)
- 2025-02-13 added telemetry correlation and command recipes (Miguel S.)
- 2025-02-14 runbook draft and action item assignments (Asha M., Priya K.)

Unresolved: move to postmortem ticket SRE-5172 for full RCA and signal baseline adjustments.
